tests.name: Numerical Reasoning Test 8
tests.subtitle: AssessmentDay source test
tests.description: A 30-question AssessmentDay numerical reasoning practice test covering mixed data interpretation, arithmetic, ratios, percentages, and financial reasoning.
tests.instructions:
This numerical reasoning test comprises 30 questions, and you will have 30 minutes in
which to correctly answer as many as you can. Calculators are permitted for this test, and it is
recommended you have some rough paper to work on.

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the
answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have
five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to
review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will
automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep
working until the time limit is up.

Try to find a time and place where you will not be interrupted during the test. The test will
begin on the next page.

questions.prompt: What was a Japanese Yen worth in Euros in Week 3?
How much is 5,000 South African Rand worth in Week 4 in US $?
In Week two 10,000 Japanese Yen is converted into £. In Week 5 this is converted into what value in Euros?

During Week 1 a traveller splits £2,100 equally into US $, Japanese Yen and South African Rand. How many £ does the traveller have on Week 3 if all the currencies are converted back into £ and he is charged a 5% fee for each transaction from one currency into another (to the nearest £100)?
questions.explanation: Each currency receives £700. After the first 5% fee, £665 is exchanged. Converting back in Week 3 and deducting the second 5% gives: dollars £665 × (1.64 ÷ 1.74) × 0.95 = £595.17; yen £665 × (123.2 ÷ 134.8) × 0.95 = £577.37; rand £665 × (13.4 ÷ 13.2) × 0.95 = £641.94. Total = £1,814.48, which rounds to £1,800 to the nearest £100.

questions.prompt: Which currency has shown the greatest proportionate change in value between Weeks 1 and 4?
questions.explanation: Compare absolute proportional rate changes from Week 1 to Week 4: euro (1.34−1.20)/1.20 = 11.67%; US dollar (1.84−1.64)/1.64 = 12.20%; yen (135−123.2)/123.2 = 9.58%; rand (13.6−13.4)/13.4 = 1.49%. The US dollar changes most.

questions.prompt: Next Year’s turnover projection for Consultancies A-E combined represents what proportional change on Year 4’s turnover for Consultancies A-E?
questions.explanation: Year 4 total = 24+35+24+22+26 = 131 units. Projected total = 22+26+35+24+30 = 137 units. Proportional change = (137−131) ÷ 131 × 100 = 4.58%, which rounds to 4.6%.

questions.prompt: If, in Year 3, Consultancies A to E represent 60% of the marketplace by value of sales, what is the value of the marketplace excluding Consultancies A-E?
questions.explanation: Year 3 turnover is (26+28+30+18+27) × €100,000 = €12.9 million. If that is 60%, the whole market is €12.9m ÷ 0.60 = €21.5m. Excluding A–E leaves 40%: €21.5m−€12.9m = €8.6 million.

questions.prompt: The turnover target for Consultancy B over the 5 year period shown is €16.5 million. By how much does turnover need to exceed Next Year’s Projected turnover in order for the target to be met?
questions.explanation: Consultancy B earned €3.0m+€3.3m+€2.8m+€3.5m = €12.6m in Years 1–4. It therefore needs €16.5m−€12.6m = €3.9m next year. The projection is €2.6m, so it must exceed it by €3.9m−€2.6m = €1.3 million.

questions.prompt: Next year, which company is projecting the smallest percentage change in its turnover?
questions.explanation: Absolute projected changes from Year 4 are: A |22−24|/24 = 8.33%; B = 25.71%; C = 45.83%; D = 9.09%; E = 15.38%. Consultancy A has the smallest percentage change.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of Year 3’s Consultancy C’s turnover to Consultancy E’s turnover?
questions.explanation: In Year 3, Consultancy C is 30 units and E is 27 units. The ratio 30:27 simplifies by dividing both sides by 3 to 10:9.

questions.prompt: What % of total plasma TV sales are made online?
questions.explanation: Catalogue plasma-TV sales are 30% of £250,000 = £75,000. Total plasma-TV sales are £75,000+£325,000+£456,000 = £856,000. Online share = £325,000 ÷ £856,000 × 100 = 37.97%, or 38%.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in value between total sales for IPods compared to cameras?
questions.explanation: Catalogue sales are £45,000 for IPods (18% of £250,000) and £40,000 for cameras (16%). Total IPod sales = £45,000+£852,000+£644,000 = £1,541,000. Total camera sales = £40,000+£553,000+£336,000 = £929,000. Difference = £612,000.

questions.prompt: If the High Street and Catalogue sales of DVD Players had been made online, what % of total Online sales would DVD Players represent?

In 2012 total Catalogue sales are forecast to increase by 1/4, total Online sales to increase by a 1/5th, and High Street sales to decrease by 12%. What will be the 2012 sales for Catalogue, Online and High Street combined (to the nearest £1,000)?
The profit made from selling cameras online compared to the High Street is in the ratio 9:7, and 15% of online camera sales is profit. What is the 2011 profit for High Street camera sales?
questions.explanation: Online camera profit = £553,000×15% = £82,950. With online:High Street profit = 9:7, High Street profit = £82,950×7/9 = £64,516.67, which rounds to £64,517.

questions.prompt: Which Department has the highest expense budget per member of staff?
questions.explanation: Annual budget per person is HR £6,500/3 = £2,166.67; Marketing £16,000/6 = £2,666.67; Sales £22,500/12 = £1,875; IT £4,500/5 = £900; Finance £20,000/7 = £2,857.14. Finance is highest.

questions.prompt: If the annual expense budget was evenly allocated for each Quarter, which Department is under budget by the highest amount in Quarter 4?
questions.explanation: Quarterly allocations minus Quarter 4 spending are: HR £1,625−£1,346 = £279; Marketing £4,000−£4,309 = −£309; Sales £5,625−£5,245 = £380; Finance £5,000−£4,463 = £537; R&D £1,500−£1,821 = −£321. Finance is under budget by the most.

questions.prompt: 60% of the Sales Department’s budgets for Quarters 1 and 4 was for attending a Sales Conference. The remainder of the budget was split equally between accommodation and travel costs. What were the Sales Department’s travel costs for Quarters 1 and 4 combined?
questions.explanation: The table gives the annual expense budget and actual quarterly expenses, but it does not state the Sales Department's budgets for Quarters 1 and 4. The annual budget cannot be assumed to be divided equally, and actual spending cannot substitute for the unknown quarterly budgets, so the travel costs cannot be determined.

questions.prompt: The Finance Department has receipts for £14,476 of its annual expenses. What percentage of the Finance Department’s annual expenses do not have receipts?

If the percentage changes in expenses that each Department exhibited between Quarters 3-4 continued into the first quarter of the next year, what would be that quarter’s total expenses (to the nearest £100)?
What was Year 2’s decrease in the amount invested in North American and European Equities compared to Year 1?
questions.explanation: Year 1 North American plus European equities = $0.4m+$0.6m = $1.0m. Year 2 values are 8% and 12% of $4.5m, totaling 20%×$4.5m = $0.9m. Decrease = $0.1m = $100,000.

questions.prompt: Which type of investment shows the largest difference between Year 1 and Year 2 in the proportion it contributed to the total Growth Fund?
questions.explanation: Year 1 shares of the $4.8m fund are Gilts 4.17%, Fixed Interest 16.67%, North American 8.33%, UK 33.33%, Pacific Rim 25%. Compare with Year 2 shares 4%, 14%, 8%, 40%, 22%: the largest absolute difference is UK Equities at 6.67 percentage points.

questions.prompt: If the proportional change in the Growth Fund between Year 1 and Year 2 continued over subsequent years, what would be the projected Growth Fund value in Year 6?
questions.explanation: The annual factor is $4.5m/$4.8m = 0.9375. From Year 2 to Year 6 there are four further periods, so Year 6 = $4.5m×0.9375⁴ = $3.4761m, or $3.48 million.

questions.prompt: If in Year 2 the amount invested in Year 1’s Fixed Interest fund had been sold and converted into European Equity funds, what is the value of European Equity funds in Year 2? (Assume no charges are incurred).
questions.explanation: Year 2 European Equities are 12%×$4.5m = $0.54m. Adding the $0.8m held in Year 1 Fixed Interest gives $0.54m+$0.8m = $1.34 million.

questions.prompt: In Year 3 the percentage of the Growth Fund held in each investment type is the same as in Year 1. The total value of the Growth Fund increases by 14% of the Year 2 value. What is the value of Year 3’s holding in UK Equities?
questions.explanation: Year 3 total = $4.5m + 14%×$4.5m = $5.13m. In Year 1, UK Equities are $1.6m/$4.8m = one third of the fund. One third of $5.13m = $1.71 million.

questions.prompt: Which month has the lowest asset turnover value? (Use the formula Asset Turnover = Total Sales / Fixed Assets)
questions.explanation: Asset turnover is Jan 136,000/38,000 = 3.579; Feb = 3.971; March = 4.266; April = 156,000/45,000 = 3.467; May = 3.625. April is lowest.

questions.prompt: Compared to May’s figures, Total sales for June show an increase of 8% and Operating expenses show a decrease of 7%. What is June’s Income?
Which month has the highest Working capital to Total assets ratio?
questions.explanation: Using (Current Assets−Liabilities)/Total Assets gives Jan 32,100/140,500 = 22.85%; Feb 27,400/132,500 = 20.68%; March 32,000/133,000 = 24.06%; April 33,000/151,000 = 21.85%; May 32,500/142,500 = 22.81%. March is highest.

questions.prompt: If the average value of Total assets between the months of April to June is £150,000, what is the value of Total assets in June?
questions.explanation: A £150,000 three-month average requires £450,000 total. June assets = £450,000−£151,000−£142,500 = £156,500.

questions.prompt: If the average monthly sales for the first five months of the year was the same for the months of June to December, what was the total annual sales?
questions.explanation: First-five-month sales total £136,000+£135,000+£136,500+£156,000+£145,000 = £708,500, so the monthly average is £141,700. If that average applies to all 12 months, annual sales = £141,700×12 = £1,700,400.

questions.prompt: If Howards and Makepeace’s annual sales target for Brand B was £690,000, what fraction of this were actual Brand B sales?
What are the average sales per quarter for each brand (in the order Brand C; B; A)?
What was Brand a’s total sales turnover for the first and second month in Quarter 4?
questions.explanation: Brand A’s Quarter 4 total is £53,000. The third month contributed £23,000, so the first two months contributed £53,000−£23,000 = £30,000.

questions.prompt: If the variable costs had been 5% higher for the previous month then what would have been the impact on Brand A’s profit?
questions.explanation: Previous-month variable costs were £5,500. A 5% increase is £5,500×0.05 = £275; with turnover and other costs unchanged, profit decreases by £275.

questions.prompt: The sales tax was calculated incorrectly for Quarter 4 Month 3 and should have been 16.5%. The mistake caused the Net Turnover for Brand A to be reported as being what?
questions.explanation: The tax used was 14% of £23,000; it should have been 16.5%. The understated tax is (16.5%−14%)×£23,000 = 2.5%×£23,000 = £575, so net turnover was reported £575 too high.

questions.prompt: Which operation achieved the highest sales per Sales and Support staff?
questions.explanation: Sales per staff are: CF Telephone £64,000/2 = £32,000; CF Catalogue £47,800/2 = £23,900; CF High Street £38,200/5 = £7,640; Callz Telephone £55,400/1 = £55,400. Callz Telephone is highest.

questions.prompt: Callz Ltd plans to reduce its staff headcount by two. The remaining staff will be split across an online team and an offline team to a ratio of 1:2. If the online group sales target is £180,000, what is the average target per member of the online team?
questions.explanation: Callz has 4+4+2+1 = 11 staff; after reducing by two it has 9. A 1:2 split puts 9×1/3 = 3 staff online. £180,000/3 = £60,000 per member.

questions.prompt: Across both companies, which retail operation had the lowest absolute difference between monthly sales and sales target?
questions.explanation: Absolute gaps are £2,500 for Callz Internet, £2,200 for CF Catalogue, £3,200 for Callz High Street, and £1,200 for Callz Catalogue. The smallest is Callz Catalogue.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of CF plc’s actual monthly telephone sales to overall monthly CF plc sales?

Following a merger, the four retail operations are combined with each other across Callz Ltd and CF plc. The targets are also combined for each retail operation, with 5% added to each target for each staff member that works in the combined retail operation. Which combined retail operation has a sales target of £119,000?
questions.explanation: For Internet, combined target = £40,000+£45,000 = £85,000 and combined staff = 4+4 = 8. Adding 5% per staff adds 40%, giving £85,000×1.40 = £119,000.

questions.prompt: The US operations exceeded their sales target for 2009 by 25%. If the target was split equally across 4 American regions, what was the individual sales target for each region?
questions.explanation: US sales were 51.5×£100,000 = £5.15m, equal to 125% of target. Target = £5.15m/1.25 = £4.12m. Split four ways, each region’s target was £4.12m/4 = £1.03 million.

questions.prompt: In 2009, which categories of electrical goods each sold more than £0.75 million in the UK?
questions.explanation: UK sales were 29.1×£100,000 = £2.91m. Category values are Misc 26% = £0.7566m, Computers 25% = £0.7275m, DVD players 29% = £0.8439m. Only Misc and DVD players exceed £0.75m.

questions.prompt: Tamcer Inc’s Russian business is split into 2 regions: Eastern Region and Western Region. Eastern Region’s sales were the equivalent of 300% of the Western Region’s sales. What were the Eastern Region’s sales?
questions.explanation: Russian sales were 11.0×£100,000 = £1.1m. If East = 3×West, total = 4×West, so East = 3/4×£1.1m = £825,000.

questions.prompt: If the absolute level of computers, games and cameras sold in France mirrors that of the UK, what is the total value of DVD players and Misc electrical goods sold in Tamcer’s French operations?
questions.explanation: UK computers, games and cameras are (25%+8%+12%)×£2.91m = 45%×£2.91m = £1,309,500. France total is 35.9×£100,000 = £3,590,000. The remaining DVD and Misc value is £3,590,000−£1,309,500 = £2,280,500.

questions.prompt: The total worldwide sales for Tamcer Inc. are £29 million. What level of sales is accounted for by countries other than those shown?

If instead of being introduced in full next year, the budget salary increases are phased in over the next three years (at a rate of 2% per year), what will be the average United States Director’s salary in 2 years time?

Next year the rise in budget for a Spanish Director's average salary will be achieved through two consecutive pay-rises. If the first pay-rise is an increase of 2%, what will the second percentage increase have to be?
questions.explanation: The two rises must produce the 5% budget factor: 1.02×(1+r) = 1.05. Thus r = 1.05/1.02−1 = 0.02941 = 2.94%, shown as 2.9%.

questions.prompt: Directors and managers are allowed to purchase company shares (price = £4.50) in place of salary next year. Which country’s average Director can buy the most number of shares, and which country has the most managers who can buy shares?
questions.explanation: Next-year director salaries are UK £95,680; France £102,060; Germany £125,080; US £121,900; Spain £88,200, so Germany buys the most £4.50 shares. Manager totals are UK 340, France 385, Germany 475, US 540, Spain 465, so the United States has the most managers.

questions.prompt: Put the countries in order of decreasing numbers of managers.
options: United States, Spain, Germany, France, United Kingdom
Spain, United States, Germany, France, United Kingdom
United States, Germany, Spain, United Kingdom, France
United States, Germany, Spain, France, United Kingdom
questions.explanation: Add female and male managers: United States 250+290 = 540; Germany 245+230 = 475; Spain 225+240 = 465; France 175+210 = 385; United Kingdom 160+180 = 340. Decreasing order is US, Germany, Spain, France, UK.

questions.prompt: Which two countries have the same absolute difference in the number of female and male managers?
questions.explanation: Absolute female–male gaps are UK 20, France 35, Germany 15, United States 40, Spain 15. Germany and Spain both have a gap of 15.

questions.prompt: The HR Director at Shevinshaw’s Ltd conducts a survey. An eighth of the full-time HR employees state that they would prefer to work part-time. If this occurred and other staff numbers remained the same, what would be the total number of part-time employees for this year?
questions.explanation: One eighth of 56 full-time HR employees is 7. Current part-time employees across all functions total 12 + 21 + 14 + 15 + 20 = 82. Moving those 7 HR employees to part-time gives 82 + 7 = 89 part-time employees in total.

questions.prompt: Which function is forecast to lose the same number of employees as it lost last year?
questions.explanation: Current totals are Marketing 66, Finance 98, Research 60, Sales 91, HR 114. Last-year losses were Finance 104−98 = 6, Research 74−60 = 14, and HR 122−114 = 8. Forecast losses are Finance 98−90 = 8 and HR 114−96 = 18; no function loses the same number in both periods.

questions.prompt: Which function has the lowest ratio of full-time employees compared to part-time employees and freelance employees combined?
questions.explanation: Ratios are Marketing 34/(12+20) = 1.063; Finance 45/(21+32) = 0.849; Research 35/(14+11) = 1.400; HR 56/(20+38) = 0.966. Finance is lowest.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Total Sales employees outnumber total HR
HR has the most freelance employees
questions.explanation: Totals are Finance 98, Sales 91, HR 114, and Research 60, so A–C are false. Freelancers are Marketing 20, Finance 32, Research 11, Sales 24, HR 38; HR has the most, so D is true.

questions.prompt: Weekend overtime is paid at a rate of double pay for Marketing and Research employees, with other employees receiving time and a half. Which function will work the second highest number of overtime hours – assuming that each employee works 8 days per year overtime – next year?
questions.explanation: Because every employee works the same 8 overtime days, overtime hours rank exactly with projected headcount. Next-year projections are HR 96, Sales 94, Finance 90, Marketing 76, Research 72. Sales is second highest.

questions.prompt: In which month shown did house prices change the most, and the least, respectively?
questions.explanation: Compare absolute monthly changes: Jan 0.4%, Feb 0.6%, March 2.4%, April 1.6%, May 2.2%, June 0.9%, July 1.1%. March is largest and January is smallest.

questions.prompt: Which two property prices are in the ratio of 4:5?
questions.explanation: £208,000:£260,000 simplifies by dividing by £52,000 to 4:5, so the 2-bedroom flat and 3-bedroom flat form the ratio.

questions.prompt: At the end of June, a property speculator buys three 2-bedroom flats at the average price and rents each one out at £900 profit per month. If she sells the properties eighteen months later with house prices having risen 15% since purchase, how much profit, before costs, has she made?
If the cost of a 4-bedroom house continues at the same monthly rate of inflation as July, what will the cost be at the end of October?
questions.explanation: The end-of-June price is £365,000 and July inflation is 1.1%. Applying that monthly rate for July through October gives £365,000×1.011⁴ = £381,326.94, which rounds to £381,327.

questions.prompt: If a newly decorated studio flat was worth £141,400 at the start of the year, what was its value at the end of February?
questions.explanation: Apply January’s −0.4% and February’s +0.6% consecutively: £141,400×0.996×1.006 = £141,679.4064, which rounds to £141,679.
